title: Why You Need Leverage For Classroom Management… And How To Get It
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents leverage—students' genuine desire to be part of a teacher's classroom—as the foundational concept underlying effective classroom management, arguing that without it consequences become ineffective and teachers are forced into exhausting tactics like bribing, lecturing, and reminding. He provides an extensive list of ways to build leverage, including being likable, keeping a clean and organized classroom, pursuing challenging goals together, using meaningful praise, staying calm, developing students' confidence, and protecting their right to learn without interference. Rather than treating rules, consequences, and rewards as the core of classroom management, Linsin frames leverage as the underlying force that makes those tools actually work. He positions the article as an index to future site content and points readers to his book Dream Class for a fuller treatment of the topic.
points: Leverage—students' genuine desire to be part of the classroom—is the foundational force that makes consequences and classroom management work.
Without leverage, teachers are forced into exhausting, minimally effective tactics like bribing, lecturing, and reminding.
Ways to build leverage include being likable, maintaining a clean and organized classroom, using meaningful praise, and staying calm.
Rules, consequences, and rewards are secondary; leverage is what makes those tools actually effective.
Building enough leverage can make even the toughest students responsive to nothing more than a glance from the teacher.
quotes: The key to effective classroom management is leverage. If your students like being part of your classroom, then you have leverage, and accountability will work the way it’s supposed to.
Done correctly, a teacher’s leverage can become so powerful and so influential that even the toughest students need no more than a glance to curb behavior. That is no exaggeration.
Regardless of where you teach or who your students are, the power of leverage can transform your students into the class you really want.

Teachers seeking to improve classroom management tend to focus on finding the right combination of rules, consequences, and rewards that will work for them. These are important, no doubt. But what makes them go, what makes them effective, is leverage.
The idea is to create a tsunami of leverage so wide and deep that no student can resist its power.
You’ll discover your influence with students growing right along with your love of teaching and everything—classroom management, motivation, attentiveness, academic performance—becoming much easier.
